# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. Lead with what the user sees now and say why it matters to them; add an action or limit when it matters. A fix to something not yet released has no changeset. Use a short sentence for a simple change, or a short lead and bullets for related details. No internal names, mechanism or filler.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON changes that only replace string values are written into the original text by span (`json_text`), anything else keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Enforcing an invariant

Use the first rung that works:

1. A type, or a private constructor or field, so the wrong thing cannot compile.
2. An exhaustive `match` with no `_` arm on our own enums.
3. A clippy or rustc lint already in the workspace lints.
4. One small test that drives the real binary or function and checks observable behavior.
5. Nothing.

- No tests that scan source text, or grep docs or workflows for strings that code can expose directly.
- No hand-maintained lists that mirror code (error codes, command names, env names): derive them from the type.
- Prefer a crate already in `Cargo.lock` over a hand-written grammar: `semver` for versions, `miette` and `thiserror` for errors, `clap` derive for args, `serde` for formats, `insta` for snapshots.
- Every new error code, JSON key or flag is permanent after 1.0: prefer fewer, broader ones.
- Before adding a check, delete one that a type now covers.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Stability

What Callisto promises to keep working from 1.0, and what it does not. A breaking change to anything in the first table needs a major version.

## Stable

| Surface | The promise |
| --- | --- |
| The eight commands (`add`, `status`, `version`, `pre`, `snapshot`, `init`, `release`, `completions`) and their flags | A flag keeps its meaning; a new flag never changes what the command did without it. |
| Exit codes | `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error: a bad or missing argument or flag, including values the command validates after parsing; the same value read from `callisto.toml`, a changeset or another file is a failure, not a usage error. |
| `--format json` reports | Every report carries `schemaVersion`. Within a version a field is not removed, renamed or retyped; fields may be added. A shape change bumps the version. `release inspect` prints the intent, manifest or receipt unchanged: its own `schemaVersion`, no `command` or `dryRun`. `schema` prints JSON Schema documents, not reports. |
| `callisto.toml` | A key keeps its meaning. Unknown keys are an error, so a new key arrives in a minor release and never changes an existing file's behavior. |
| Changesets | The `.changeset/*.md` format and `pre.json` stay compatible with `@changesets/cli`. The bare package name is the key unless another ecosystem has a package of that name, in which case the key is `ecosystem/name`. |
| Error codes | A code keeps naming the same condition and is never reused. New codes may appear. |
| Tag names | `{name}@{version}` by default, `ecosystem/name@{version}` once another ecosystem has a package of that name. Pin a name with `tag-template` if a stable tag matters to your tooling. |
| The GitHub Actions | The inputs of `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto`. The floating `v1` tag moves only on stable releases; pin a commit for a fixed version. |

## CI plumbing

The generated workflows use `release plan`, `release inspect`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release build-python`, `release-pr`, `matrix`, `compose-pr-body` and `schema`. They are hidden from `--help` and work only with the same Callisto version that generated them: the intent, decision, receipt and run envelope carry versions, and a reader rejects any other. Keep the action and the binary on one version, and regenerate with `callisto init` after an upgrade.

## Not covered

- Text output, stderr, warnings and the wording of error messages.
- The library crates (`callisto-model`, `-manifests`, `-graph`). They are internal and version in lockstep with the CLI.
- The order of keys in JSON output, and timing or performance.
- Platforms without a published binary. Windows is not supported.
# Architecture decision records

- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.
- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — proposed v1 model with some behavior already implemented. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.

## Rules

- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.
- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI, including napi-rs layouts. Co-located Cargo/Maturin is after v1; separate-directory Cargo and Python packages are supported. Go and NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Native tools and CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform or cross-registry transaction.
- Committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only `execute` receives registry secrets; the repo has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate.
- Each implementation PR updates the affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic.

- npm JSON layout normalization, and the scope of napi `.node` attestation.
- External items: rust-cache pin, bot-PR check policy, token rotation and the retired-crate migration notices.

OIDC trusted publishing ([plan](OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md)), `cargo-semver-checks` on the promised surfaces (schema output, config and report formats), and a review of the remaining `expect` calls.

# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. The evidence is in `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

# Specifications

Each spec (`spec@1`) states current behavior as testable criteria, grouped by topic prefix. No history: Git records how the behavior got here, and [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md) records the design decisions that still hold.

| Spec | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [`workspace.json`](workspace.json) | Root and member discovery, package identity, per-package config rules, npm platform packages |
| [`versioning.json`](versioning.json) | Changeset format, severity aggregation, cascade, groups, prerelease, snapshot, applying versions, changelogs, the release decision file |
| [`release.json`](release.json) | `callisto release`, the CI route, decision authority, operation order, registry publish and observation, reruns, tags and GitHub releases, the managed release PR |
| [`cli.json`](cli.json) | Command surface, output and exit codes, `status`, `add`, `init`, generated workflows, `pre`, `snapshot`, `completions`, `schema` |
| [`matrix.json`](matrix.json) | `callisto matrix`: native build targets and runtime constraints for CI |

`REQ-DX-V1.md` is the open v1 requirement; delete it when v1 ships.

How the code implements these specs: [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`docs/architecture/`](../architecture/).

When code and a spec disagree, reproduce the behavior first. Fix the spec if the intended contract changed; otherwise fix the code.

Remaining v1 work is in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). Behavior not yet implemented, such as co-located Cargo/Maturin version derivation, lives in [the scoped design](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Amend the matching current-behavior spec in the same change that implements it; the design does not make future behavior current.

# Configuration reference

Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).

This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.

## Top-level tables

| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[changelog]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |

Example: `layout = "flat"`.

#!/bin/zsh
# usage: mkfix.sh DIR
set -e
D=$1
rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D/crates/a/src $D/crates/b/src $D/web $D/py $D/.changeset
cd $D
git init -q -b main
git config user.email t@t.t; git config user.name t; git config commit.gpgsign false
cat > Cargo.toml <<'E'
[workspace]
members = ["crates/a", "crates/b"]
resolver = "2"
E
cat > crates/a/Cargo.toml <<'E'
[package]
name = "a"
version = "1.2.0"
edition = "2021"
E
cat > crates/b/Cargo.toml <<'E'
[package]
name = "b"
version = "0.3.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
a = { path = "../a", version = "1.2.0" }
E
echo 'pub fn f(){}' > crates/a/src/lib.rs; echo 'pub fn g(){}' > crates/b/src/lib.rs
cat > package.json <<'E'
{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["web"] }
E
cat > web/package.json <<'E'
{
  "name": "web",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "weblib": "^1.0.0" }
}
E
cat > py/pyproject.toml <<'E'
[project]
name = "pylib"
version = "0.1.0"
E
cat > callisto.toml <<'E'
[release]
forge-repository = "o/r"
E
echo '{"version":1}' > /dev/null
cargo generate-lockfile -q --offline 2>/dev/null || true
git add -A; git commit -qm init
git tag a@1.2.0; git tag b@0.3.0

set -e

rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D/crates/a/src $D/crates/b/src $D/web $D/py $D/.changeset
cd $D
/usr/bin/git init -q -b main
/usr/bin/git config user.email t@t.t; /usr/bin/git config user.name t; /usr/bin/git config commit.gpgsign false; /usr/bin/git config tag.gpgsign false; /usr/bin/git config tag.forceSignAnnotated false
cat > Cargo.toml <<'E'
[workspace]
members = ["crates/a", "crates/b"]
resolver = "2"
E
cat > crates/a/Cargo.toml <<'E'
[package]
name = "a"
version = "1.2.0"
edition = "2021"
E
cat > crates/b/Cargo.toml <<'E'
[package]
name = "b"
version = "0.3.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
a = { path = "../a", version = "1.2.0" }
E
echo 'pub fn f(){}' > crates/a/src/lib.rs; echo 'pub fn g(){}' > crates/b/src/lib.rs
cat > package.json <<'E'
{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["web"] }
E
cat > web/package.json <<'E'
{
  "name": "web",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "weblib": "^1.0.0" }
}
E
cat > py/pyproject.toml <<'E'
[project]
name = "pylib"
version = "0.1.0"
E
cat > callisto.toml <<'E'
[release]
forge-repository = "o/r"
E
echo '{"version":1}' > /dev/null
cargo generate-lockfile -q --offline 2>/dev/null || true
/usr/bin/git add -A; /usr/bin/git commit -qm init
/usr/bin/git tag -a a@1.2.0 -m a; /usr/bin/git tag -a b@0.3.0 -m b

description: 'Creates or updates a Callisto release PR; durable execution belongs to the repository workflow'
inputs:
  version_command:
    description: 'Version command; defaults to callisto version, which refreshes lockfiles. Callisto appends --emit-decision <decision_path>. The value is split on whitespace, so it cannot contain quoted arguments or a path with spaces.'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto version'
  decision_path:
    description: 'Path, relative to cwd, where the version command records the exact release decision this PR carries. Committed alongside the manifest and changelog edits; `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` verifies the merged commit against this file rather than re-deriving release policy.'
    required: false
    default: '.callisto/release-decision.json'
  commit_message:
    description: 'Release-PR commit message'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  title:
    description: 'Release-PR title'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  pr_label:
    description: 'Release-PR label'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto: release'
  branch:
    description: 'Base branch for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'main'
  release_branch:
    description: 'Branch managed for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto/version-packages'
  github_token:
    description: 'Optional GitHub token for pull-request and forge commit API operations. The managed branch is never pushed with `git push`; the default GITHUB_TOKEN is sufficient even on a public repository, since the executor never writes `.github/workflows/*`.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  setup_callisto:
    description: 'Install the Callisto environment before running'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's own
      invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling back to
      the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  cwd:
    description: 'Workspace directory'
    required: false
    default: '.'
  mode:
    description: 'version-pr (default): create/update the release PR. release: run `callisto release`.'
    required: false
    default: 'version-pr'
outputs:
  hasChangesets:
    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found (mode: version-pr only)'
    value: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}
  published:

  publishedPackages:
    description: 'JSON array of packages `callisto release` published (mode: release only; otherwise [])'
    value: ${{ steps.release.outputs.publishedPackages || '[]' }}

content.content:
name: Hold release PR

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions: {}

# One hold at a time, so concurrent runs never both create the state comment; a newer push replaces a queued run.
concurrency:
  group: hold-release-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  hold:
    name: Hold the release PR until it is refreshed
    timeout-minutes: 5
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Draft the open release PR
        run: bash .github/scripts/hold-release-pr.sh callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drafts the open managed release PR when main moves, so a stale one cannot be merged before the release workflow refreshes it.
# Usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>; needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
set -euo pipefail

release_branch="${1:?usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>}"

prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,headRefName,headRepository)
numbers=$(jq -r --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg branch "$release_branch" '
  .[] | select(.isDraft == false
    and (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // "") == $repo
    and (.headRefName == $branch or (.headRefName | startswith($branch + "--")))) | .number' <<< "$prs")

for number in $numbers; do

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions: {}

# One hold at a time, so concurrent runs never both create the state comment; a newer push replaces a queued run.
concurrency:
  group: hold-release-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  hold:
    name: Hold the release PR until it is refreshed
    timeout-minutes: 5
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Draft the open release PR
        run: bash .github/scripts/hold-release-pr.sh callisto/version-packages

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drafts the open managed release PR when main moves, so a stale one cannot be merged before the release workflow refreshes it.
# Usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>; needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
set -euo pipefail

release_branch="${1:?usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>}"

prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,headRefName,headRepository)
numbers=$(jq -r --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg branch "$release_branch" '
  .[] | select(.isDraft == false
    and (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // "") == $repo
    and (.headRefName == $branch or (.headRefName | startswith($branch + "--")))) | .number' <<< "$prs")

  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if gh pr ready "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --undo; then
      echo "::notice::Held release PR #$number as a draft until the release workflow refreshes it"
      break
    fi
    [[ $attempt -lt 3 ]] || { echo "::error::could not draft release PR #$number"; exit 1; }
    sleep $((attempt * 2))
  done
done

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Finding releases that did not finish

`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

```sh
callisto release pending                    # text
callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
```

Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.

If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Finding releases that did not finish

`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

```sh
callisto release pending                    # text
callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
```

Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.

If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh

callisto-cli: patch

== .changeset/camel-case-json-fields.md
---
callisto-cli: minor
---

Every JSON field Callisto writes is now camelCase, so scripts see one naming style.

- `version` and `snapshot` `--format json` reports: `reason.dep_kind` and `reason.dependency_to` are now `depKind` and `dependencyTo`.

== .changeset/catch-bad-input-early.md
---
callisto-cli: minor
---

Mistyped config keys and pre-release tags are caught where you make them.

- An unknown key inside a `[[fixed-group]]` or `[[linked-group]]` block now fails with an error naming the key. Before, it was silently ignored.
- `callisto pre enter` rejects a tag with a space, `!`, `/`, an empty part or a number with a leading zero such as `01` (E324) and writes nothing. Before, it wrote `pre.json` and `version` failed later with a confusing version error. Dotted tags such as `beta.

- `pre-major-inference = "false"` is rejected (E256). It was accepted as `off` but never documented; use `"off"`.

Action: if a group block in `callisto.toml` carries a key Callisto does not recognise, remove it, and replace `pre-major-inference = "false"` with `"off"`.

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) lists the verification and onboarding work that remains. Real local npm, Cargo and PyPI tests exist; the Cargo and PyPI ones drive the publisher directly and do not cover registry binding or observation.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- A verified defect is fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. The real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests fail, not skip, under CI when a tool is missing, and production binding/observation paths are checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, and dual Cargo/npm outputs. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan/build jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

## Out of scope

- Non-GitHub forges (later).
- Moon plugin (replaced by a proto plugin separately).
- Crate consolidation / license split.
- Production Go or NuGet adapters, arbitrary SCM-derived Python version backends, automatic foreign-registry dependency inference and cross-registry atomic rollback.

fix(release): do not tag a published version onto a later commit | MERGED
perf(release): plan a large release with a fixed number of git processes
## Summary

Planning a release in a very large monorepo scaled with the number of releasing packages, so `callisto release` and the release PR body slowed sharply as more packages shipped together. Two causes, found by the same benchmark on one planning path:

- The preflight that checks a package has not moved past its version commit ran one `git log` and one `git cat-file --batch` per package. It now runs one `git log` for all manifests (`first_parent_commits_by_path` in `callisto-model`, using `--first-parent -m` and literal pathspecs) plus one batched read. A package whose newest candidate is not the version-setting commit falls back to its own read, so results are unchanged.
- `workspace_package` rescanned every package and recomputed identities on each call. It is replaced by a map built once (`ReleaseOwners`), every call site is migrated, and per-selection linear scans are now set lookups.

Measured on a synthetic monorepo (1,800 packages, 1,500 depending on one core package, 1,000 pending changesets, 20,000 tags): `release --dry-run` 13.9 s to 1.85 s and 3,012 git processes to 14 (debug), 8.10 s to 1.27 s (release build). With 20,000 commits it goes from 7.95 s to 1.63 s, and `compose-pr-body` from 12.1 s to 1.45 s (debug) and 1.90 s to 0.76 s (release). `status`, `version --dry-run` and the other dimensions benchmarked flat or linear and are untouched.

## Verify

Old and new output are byte-identical for `release --dry-run` text and JSON and for `compose-pr-body` on both large cases.

A counting-runner test pins one `git log` and a bounded `cat-file` count at 3 and at 12 packages, and two mutations fail it. The existing version-commit tests, including a 105-edit and merge-commit cases, pass. A wall-clock test for the lookup map was dropped as flaky; the map is covered by the selection tests.

`just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and `just workflow-contracts` exit 0. CI has not run.

Not changed: `version --emit-preview` takes 33 to 45 s when thousands of packages are bumped, about 75% of it macOS `F_FULLFSYNC` from the per-file and per-directory fsync. That is the durability invariant in AGENTS.md, so it is left alone.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Moves the floating major tag (v1, v2, ...) to a release commit, for a stable release at or past 1.0.0.
# Run inside the release-source checkout, after the release succeeded, so `uses: ...@v1` follows the newest 1.x.
# Usage: move-floating-tag.sh <release-decision.json> <package> <commit> [remote]
set -euo pipefail

decision="${1:?usage: move-floating-tag.sh <release-decision.json> <package> <commit> [remote]}"
package="${2:?missing package}"
commit="${3:?missing commit}"
remote="${4:-origin}"

if [[ ! "$commit" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
  echo "::error::commit must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
  exit 1
fi

version=$(jq -r --arg package "$package" '[.entries[] | select(.package == $package) | .targetVersion][0] // empty' "$decision")
if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
  echo "$package is not in this release; no floating tag to move"
  exit 0
fi
if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^([0-9]+)\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "$version is not a stable X.Y.Z version; no floating tag to move"
  exit 0
fi
major="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
if ((major < 1)); then
  echo "$version is before 1.0.0; no floating tag to move"
  exit 0
fi
tag="v$major"

current=$(git ls-remote --tags "$remote" "refs/tags/$tag" | awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }')
if [[ "$current" == "$commit" ]]; then
  echo "$tag already points at $commit"
  exit 0
fi
if [[ -n "$current" ]]; then
  # A recovery run of an older release must not drag the tag backwards.
  git fetch --quiet "$remote" "refs/tags/$tag:refs/tags/$tag" --force

input.message:
Verified against origin/main 828475eba (0.19.0 released; 0.20 release PR #493 open, it carries a large batch of breaking JSON/error-code churn). I read the code and docs, ran the binary on a temp Cargo+npm+PyPI fixture, and ran the bench. Nothing was edited, committed or pushed. I did not run `just ci` or the test suite. I could not run `init` or `release` with registry access: the sandbox blocks the network, and `release --dry-run` fails with E176 when it cannot reach a registry. A separate session switched my worktree twice; I only read other worktrees.

**Ranked 1.0 blockers**

1. **No golden for the JSON report shapes.** stability.md promises that, within a `schemaVersion`, no field is removed, renamed or retyped. `schema_guard_test.rs` pins the top-level fields of the status report only, plus enum variant sets (`DiagnosticCode`, operation roles, observation enums). The other schemas are generated from the same types as the output, so a rename passes. Reports in use today: add=1, pre=1, release pending=1, errors=1, status/version/snapshot/matrix=2. An open PR (#526) is already bumping one to 3. Smallest fix: an `insta` snapshot of every `callisto schema --type` output, so any shape change is a reviewable diff. After that, the camelCase walker test and `Report::schema_version` already cover the rest.

2. **Exit 1 vs 2 is a hand-kept list.** `exit_kind` in `callisto-cli/src/error.rs` and `callisto-graph/src/error.rs` ends in `_ => Runtime`. `ConfigError::exit_kind` decides by `context.starts_with("--")`. A new flag-value error silently exits 1; that is exactly what #523 just fixed. I found two live cases:
   - `release pending --decision ../x` exits 1 with a raw E051 git error. It should be a usage error (exit 2).
   - `version --emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` accept paths outside the workspace and write there; the code does not contain them.

   Smallest fix: make the matches exhaustive with no `_` arm (AGENTS.md rung 2), and validate `--decision` the way `release plan` does.

3. **The `callisto-action` contract is unpinned.** There are 12 inputs and 3 outputs. Inputs are snake_case and outputs camelCase, which freezes on `@v1`. Several look internal: `version_command` (split on whitespace), `decision_path`, `setup_callisto`, `release_branch`. No test or doc pins any of them. Smallest fix: trim or hide the internal inputs, or state in stability.md exactly which ones are promised.

4. **`release pending` is not classified.** It shows in `release --help` and is used by the release workflow. stability.md names it neither among the eight commands nor in the CI plumbing list. Either hide it and list it as plumbing, or promise it.

5. **ADR 12 is still `Proposed`** although it is implemented: E316 and E317 are enforced and tags follow it. The README says "proposed… some behavior implemented", and ADR 11's selector-promotion half is revised without a supersede. This is an owner decision. The smallest action is to flip ADR 12 to Accepted and record what remains of ADR 11.

6. **The first `v1` tag has never run for real.** The floating-tag script returns early below 1.0.0 and no `v*` tag exists, so the 1.0.0 release is its first production run. The script is tested only against a local remote. Rehearse it, or make sure you can fix `v1` by hand.

**Can follow 1.0**

- Error codes: 276 live codes, and "never reused" for the 7 retired codes is doc-only, no test.
- The kebab-case diagnostic codes (24) are a second registry that stability.md does not mention.
- `--dry-run` is a global flag shown on read-only commands (`status`, `matrix`, `pending`), where it is a no-op. It freezes by accident.
- `release-trigger = "auto"`: `release-pr decide` returns noop with no changesets, so inference-only releases never get a managed release PR (the open ADR 2 question). `version` also prints "No pending changesets" next to a computed plan. Document the limit in config.md or leave it.
- Cargo/PyPI production-path registry tests (the registry endpoint rejects non-https URLs, loopback included).
- The under-ten-minute onboarding measurement.
- The matrix target table with its own 18 triples.
- Adopting michi-graph 0.9's `ready_by_edge`/`Needs` (0.9.0 has it; replaces `eligible_in` and `is_registry_effect`; internal).
- OIDC, private/HTML-only PyPI, channel promotion, checksums, wrapper bump severity.
- At 1.0, housekeeping: delete `REQ-DX-V1.md` and `ROAD-TO-V1.md`, and change the README's "pre-v1" line.

**Spec drift (item 4)**
I tested about 45 criteria from versioning.json, matrix.json and release.json against the binary and found no behavioral drift. Covered: CS-03/04/05/08, AGG-02/03/06, CAS-04, GRP-02/03, PRE-01 to 07, APPLY-06/07A/09 to 13/17, MX-OUT-01 to 04, MX-DISC-01 to 07, MX-ERR-01/02/07, REL-CMD-05/06/08, REL-AUTH-04, REL-ERR-02. Not tested: anything needing a registry or GitHub. Two wording gaps:
- VER-CS-04/05 cite E040 to E047, but the user sees only the wrapping E210.
- VER-AGG-06's "No pending changesets" warning also appears alongside inferred bumps.

**Release safety (item 3)**
- The "Ready for review" override is still a gap by design. The hold workflow only drafts the PR, nothing blocks a manual un-draft, and docs/releasing.md covers recovery. It can follow 1.0.
- The E165 help and docs change is shipped. The code help and docs/errors.md both name the stale-PR recovery.

**Performance (item 5)**
Release bench, 1m53s build:

| Packages | status | version --dry-run | release --dry-run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 222 ms | 219 ms | 222 ms |
| 1,800 | 820 ms | 733 ms | 581 ms |

Each command starts at most 11 git processes. This bench's workspace shape is not PR #507's (1,500 of 1,800 packages releasing), so 581 ms vs 1.3 s is not like for like.

**Stale items already done**
- Private workspace root listed as a package: fixed (changeset `skip-private-workspace-root`).
- #290 guard gaps: #290 is merged; #507 added `first_parent_commits_by_path` with 105-edit and merge-commit tests. I did not re-run them.
- michi 0.6 wait: now 0.9.
- E320, E318, snapshot refusal, floating tag, and per-distribution ordering all work or are present.
- "Spec drift ~14%": not reproduced.
- Open PRs are now #526, #495 (draft) and #493 (the release PR).
- `gh issue list` returns no open issues.
- The E194 shared-tag/release-title design pass is still open (not re-verified in code).

Evidence locations (not files I changed): `/tmp/claude-501/t1.sh` through `t11.sh` and `/tmp/claude-501/bench.out`.
